senate.title: U.S. Senate
senate.one: Votes on national laws, approves federal judges and cabinet members, and approves treaties. Texas has two senators.
senate.why: One of only 100 votes on every law in the country.

house.title: U.S. House
house.one: Votes on national laws, and speaks for your district in Washington.
house.why: Your closest voice in Washington, and you get to keep or replace them every two years.

governor.title: Governor
governor.one: Runs the state, signs or vetoes every bill the legislature passes, and appoints many state officials and judges.
governor.why: Shapes how Texas handles schools, the border, the power grid, and state spending.
also: Can veto single spending items out of the budget
Can call the legislature back for a special session

ltgov.title: Lieutenant Governor
ltgov.one: Leads the Texas Senate: decides which senators sit on which committees and which bills come up for a vote.
ltgov.why: One of the most powerful jobs in Texas, because so much of what passes runs through the Senate.
also: You vote for this office separately from governor
Takes over if the governor can't serve

ag.title: Attorney General
ag.one: Texas's top lawyer. Represents the state in court and gives legal advice to state agencies.
ag.why: Goes after scams and companies that mislead customers, and collects child support.
also: Brings lawsuits for the state against the federal government and companies

comptroller.title: Comptroller of Public Accounts
comptroller.one: Texas's tax collector and accountant. Collects state taxes and pays the state's bills.
comptroller.why: Tells the legislature how much money it can spend, so it can't pass a budget bigger than that estimate.
also: Returns lost or forgotten money (old bank accounts, uncashed checks) to its owners

land.title: Commissioner of the General Land Office
land.one: Manages the land and minerals the state owns. Money from it goes to Texas public schools.
land.why: Also runs programs for veterans' land and home loans, cares for the coast, and manages the Alamo.

agr.title: Commissioner of Agriculture
agr.one: Runs the Texas Department of Agriculture, which supports farms and ranches and oversees school lunch programs.
agr.why: Also checks that gas pumps and store scales give you what you pay for.

rrc.title: Railroad Commissioner
rrc.one: Despite the name, the Railroad Commission doesn't oversee railroads. It regulates Texas's oil and gas industry.
rrc.why: Its rules cover drilling, pipelines, and natural gas utilities, which affect jobs, land, and energy prices.
also: Three commissioners, one elected every two years

sen.title: State Senate
sen.one: Writes Texas's laws and passes the state budget. There are 31 state senators.
sen.why: State laws cover schools, property taxes, criminal law, and voting rules.
also: About half the seats are up in each election

rep.title: State House
rep.one: The other half of the legislature. There are 150 state representatives, each with a smaller district than a senator's.
rep.why: Every bill has to pass here and in the State Senate before the governor can sign it.
